title: `round` of a float keeps its type and gives +0.0; `floor` and `ceil` of a FLOAT return a `BIGINT`
verdict: `round` and `bround`: no conversion, `-0.4` and `-0.0` give `+0.0`; `floor` and `ceil`: a `BIGINT`, NaN is 0, `±inf` and values past 64 bits saturate (ANSI off) or raise ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW (ANSI on), as for DOUBLE
description: `round(a)` and `bround(a)` of a `FLOAT` stay `FLOAT` and of a `DOUBLE` stay `DOUBLE` (no `float_to_int`): `round(-0.4)` and `round(-0.0)` are `+0.0` (`round_zero_sign` is POSITIVE), as spark-round has them for doubles.

`floor(a)` and `ceil(a)` of a `FLOAT` return a `BIGINT`, as for a `DOUBLE` (spark-floor-ceil-bigint): `ceil(-0.4F)` is `0` and `CAST(ceil(-0.4F) AS DOUBLE)` is `+0.0`, `floor(-0.0F)` is `0`. NaN gives `0`; with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` off `+inf` and `3e38F` give `9223372036854775807`; with it on, a query holding them raises ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW.
reference: `round`, `floor` and `ceil` are floats to floats; the sign of a zero result is `round_zero_sign`, left open by the reference (`eval` gives `+0.0`), and `float_to_int` is Spark's conversion that the writer casts back (`Profile.spark`: `round_zero_sign` POSITIVE, `float_to_int`). The FLOAT results agree with `Profile.spark`; nothing contradicts it.

provenance.checked_by: session #746 (Spark facts), sverify_dev.probe_spark on homelab, Spark 4.3.0 local session

evidence.sql: SELECT a, round(a), bround(a), floor(a), ceil(a), typeof(round(a)), typeof(floor(a)), typeof(ceil(a)), CAST(ceil(a) AS DOUBLE) FROM VALUES (CAST(-0.4 AS FLOAT)), (-CAST(0 AS FLOAT)), (CAST(0.5 AS FLOAT)), (CAST(-2.5 AS FLOAT)) AS s(a)
SELECT floor(CAST(NaN AS FLOAT)), ceil(CAST(NaN AS FLOAT)), floor(CAST(Infinity AS FLOAT)), ceil(CAST(3e38 AS FLOAT))
evidence.observed: ANSI off: (0, 0, 9223372036854775807, 9223372036854775807); ANSI on: error ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW

evidence.note: constructs float-round-floor, float-floor-nonfinite; the double rows are double-round and double-floor-ceil
